feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible public-sector experience, and good evidence of scope across platforms, governance, analytics, and multimedia. It reads polished and substantive, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, tighter structure, and a few consistency fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership brand: the headline and summary position you well for senior digital/platform roles and align with the experience that follows.  
- Credible progression: long tenure at NACo shows steady advancement and increasing responsibility, which strengthens trust and narrative coherence.  
- Relevant technical breadth: Drupal, analytics, automation, AI-enabled search, and multimedia capabilities are well matched to modern communications leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include metrics tied to growth, efficiency, engagement, cost savings, adoption, or team performance.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve scannability and create more room for achievements.  
- Fix style consistency: punctuation and formatting vary (for example “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s”; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”). No major misspellings found, but maintain consistent bullet style, hyphenation, and capitalization throughout.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and clear seniority, but the intro is broad and repeats several competency areas already covered elsewhere. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing tied to recent public-sector leadership.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, executive language: “leading digital platforms, governance, and content operations.”
- Add one proof point from recent experience for impact, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas and reducing list-like phrasing.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web ecosystems, governance models, and content operations. Led enterprise website transformation for a 10,000+ page Drupal platform serving 3.5M annual page views, while advancing analytics, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Complex, mission-driven organizations” is accurate but generic; consider using “public-sector and membership organizations” for specificity.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and slightly more distinctive from the detailed skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, cleaner noun phrases and keep all items structurally parallel.
- Replace broader items with sharper terms tied to senior-level scope and recent work.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, swap “Cross-channel communications leadership” for “Email, web and social operations” if you want more operational specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled…,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- This section also overlaps with Topline Skills; keep competencies high-level and let later sections carry tools/platform detail.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more distinctive and scannable.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and trim stacked nouns (e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and AI chat”).
- Add one concrete signal of scale, audience, or purpose where possible (campaign audience, legislative content volume, conference/event context).
- Standardize style: spell out “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and keep punctuation/capitalization consistent across items.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in the current consulting and NACo roles.
- Consider keeping only 2–3 projects here that add specificity not already stated elsewhere, especially the anniversary campaign/display example.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and the most distinctive contributions so it complements rather than repeats the NACo entries.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-oriented line: “Redesigned cross-channel workflows, governance, and analytics to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make Drupal/CMS work more outcome-led: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits; delivered front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-visibility public web properties.”
- Keep the AI search bullet, but add a result if possible: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content models, and discovery UX to improve access to complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “digital systems/workflows” overlap with the 2022–2024 NACo role; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- The microsite and AI search bullets may duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level if those projects stay detailed in the footer.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this director-level role from the earlier NACo positions. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and systems built rather than channel management alone.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and cross-department digital operations.”
- Rewrite bullets to lead with outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more measurable where possible: add budget size, team size, reporting cadence, production volume, engagement growth, cost savings, or turnaround improvements for email/social/video/studio work.
- Combine lower-value bullets for concision: merge analytics + governance into one systems/operations bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older multimedia bullets unless framed as first-time organizational capability at director level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to the step-up in responsibility: operational ownership, editorial coordination, and channel growth.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show growth/impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make workflow/editorial bullets more active and distinct: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes linking communications, advocacy and program staff, improving publishing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video work also appears in the prior NACo role and Recent Projects; avoid repeating “first” or broad studio/build language here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tightened to emphasize leadership scope and distinctive strengths rather than restating broad digital/communications terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-value wording tied to seniority: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Editorial governance and publishing operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector and advocacy communications,” “Audience and content strategy.”
- Keep each line parallel and concise; avoid “focused”/“planning” filler.
- If space allows, make one item more distinctive to recent work, e.g. “Content operations for complex, multi-stakeholder organizations.”
- Consider reducing to 4 lines if other skills sections are dense.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill set, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, with only the most important tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to capability-led language, e.g.: **Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences**
- Remove lower-value phrasing like “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” or compress to **front-end implementation** unless the target role is hands-on developer-focused.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: **Drupal**, **CMS modernization**, **AI-enabled search**, **workflow automation**.
- If space allows, sharpen with scope language such as **enterprise web platforms** or **large public-facing sites**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the detailed tool inventory in **Technical + IT**; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies/header language, so avoid repeating the exact phrase elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application, not repeat platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business language: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and performance optimization • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development and executive reporting • SEO, user behavior and conversion analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT; keep this one strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value operational leadership and event delivery rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with a more senior, outcomes-oriented mix:  
- Broadcast-quality video production  
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery  
- In-house studio buildout and operations  
- PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows  
- Virtual event production and technical direction
- Consider changing “Video production and editing” to “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the NACo studio achievement.
- Use “technical direction” or “multi-camera workflows” if accurate; they signal leadership beyond hands-on editing.
- Keep to 4–5 bullets max and order by strategic value: event delivery/studio ops first, tools second.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- Tool-level detail here also overlaps with “Multimedia & Creative Tools” in Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS experience or expanded with level/context.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by depth and recency: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add proficiency cues instead of a plain list: **Drupal (advanced)** • **WordPress (advanced)** • **SharePoint/Power Pages (working knowledge)** • GitHub Pages
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner alignment with the rest of the CV.
- If you want more impact, replace GitHub Pages with a stronger platform/tool unless it reflects meaningful recent use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one list or making this version proficiency-based.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use version-specific naming; “HTML, CSS” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. **“front-end troubleshooting,” “CMS theming support,”** or **“deployment automation”** to better reflect current consulting/Drupal work.
- Order by relevance/strength: JavaScript, API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, HTML, CSS, jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid implying GitHub Actions overlaps with broader automation tools unless differentiated.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around systems you actively build or manage.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/most relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- Consider grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add light specificity instead of just listing tools, e.g. **Airtable system design • Power Automate workflows • Zapier integrations • Jira/Asana project operations**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” is already stated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating that exact phrase elsewhere without added specificity.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if space allows or if central to your operating model.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, especially given the recent leadership over email channels, but it’s currently just a vendor list. Make it sharper by signaling level of use and aligning it to the email/newsletter work already evidenced in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms** for clearer business relevance.
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if all three were used directly; otherwise remove any tool with limited exposure.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers: **Higher Logic (member email/newsletters) • Mailchimp (campaign email) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (CRM-linked journeys)**.
- Keep platform names concise; avoid slashes if possible: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated email-channel claims in NACo roles; don’t restate newsletter scale here unless tied to a specific platform.
- If Dynamics 365 was not central in recent work, consider dropping it to keep the list weighted toward strongest, most credible tools.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It should read as a concise technical toolkit, with sharper phrasing and less repetition of broader competency language.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to tools + methods only: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • Reporting dashboards”
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “Reporting dashboards” or “Executive reporting” for clearer business value.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recently evidenced tools from recent roles: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Power BI • Looker Studio • BigQuery …”
- If space allows elsewhere, move outcomes to experience bullets rather than this skills line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly duplicates “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider merging or making one broader and this one strictly tool-based.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are methods, not platforms; keep if you want mixed tools/methods, otherwise separate for consistency.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale or output you can add.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten and specify scope: mention 2–3 channels only, e.g., “supported web, email, social and multimedia production workflows.”
- Add measurable outputs if available: number of livestreams/video updates produced, audience growth, website refresh scope, or team size supported.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving production workflows across web, email, social and video. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the capability rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outputs, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting NACo program and policy priorities.”
- Make the digital work more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational communications and member engagement.”
- Highlight the standout achievement with stronger action verbs: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience/downloads, stakeholder groups served, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing if later roles already cover web/video/social leadership; keep this entry focused on research support + first podcast launch.
- Don’t overstate multimedia leadership here, since stronger, more recent production achievements appear in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tightening it into clearly tool-based, current production skills will make it scan better and reduce overlap with broader multimedia claims elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
